messages:
Maya: Quick proposal — want to land a per-org rate policy that combines RPM/TPM + a small concurrency cap to avoid cost spikes and thundering-herd during batch jobs. Posting a draft config and rollout idea here. :thinking:
Sam: Do you have target numbers or a model for how RPM vs TPM interacts? any calc for high-token requests?
Maya: Draft config (very rough):
```
org_rate_limit:
  rpm: 3600        # requests per minute
  tpm: 150000      # tokens per minute (counts input+output)
  concurrent: 10   # concurrent inflight requests per org
  burst_window_sec: 30
  burst_allowance: 3 # number of short bursts allowed in window
```
Maya: Behavior: concurrent is enforced at router/proxy; RPM/TMP enforced via sliding-window counters in redis. If tpm exceeded, return 429 + `Retry-After` and emit event to routing policy to consider soft-routing.
Kai: Token accounting makes sense for text-gen but embeddings are small token-wise and expensive per-request. We should allow higher RPM for embedding endpoints or treat embeddings with separate quota buckets.
Jen: Redis sliding-window is fine but watch TTL drift and race conditions. Suggest using leaky-bucket + permit-queue fallback to avoid thundering herd when counters reset. Also need deterministic ordering for queued requests to avoid starvation.
Maya: Good point. Plan: hybrid enforcement — leaky bucket for RPM, token-bucket approximation for TPM. Concurrency enforced with distributed semaphores at node-level. Queueing only used when concurrency cap hit, with a short max-wait (500ms) before 429 to keep latency SLOs.
Alex: If org hits TPM, can we route to cheaper model or dedicated pool fallback instead of 429? Some customers would prefer degraded service over errors.
Maya: Yes — routing policies will include fallback actions: `reject`, `queue`, `route:lower-tier-model`, `route:dedicated` (if reserved). We should expose per-org preference in console + API. Sample header we plan to send: `X-RateLimit-Limit: rpm=3600;tpm=150000;concurrent=10` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` + `Retry-After`.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: rate-policy/v2 pushed to staging at 2026-03-17T09:22:00Z :rocket:
Jen: Telemetry requests: need these events in metrics: rate_limit.triggered, rate_limit.action (reject/queue/route), queue_time_ms, token_consumed. Also add per-org counters for throttled_pct and throttled_latency_p95 so product can monitor regressions.
Sam: For rollout, suggest canary by org size: start with small orgs (<50 req/min) to validate counters, then top 5% low-risk customers, 25% next, full. Gradual ramp with automatic rollback if throttled_pct > 1% or error_rate spikes.
Maya: Agreed. I'll draft a console UX to expose org-level quota overrides and a simple histogram for burst events. Also adding an ops runbook for oncall: commands to inspect redis keys, force-release semaphores, and temporarily bump concurrency for customers on support calls.
Kai: One more thought — ensure our billing/tokens pipeline uses same tokenization library as rate-limiter to avoid discrepancies.
Maya: Noted. I'll include exact tokenizer hash in the rollout notes. Thanks all — I'll iterate on the numbers and post a follow-up doc with precise guardrails and dashboards. :thumbsup:
Alex: +1. Happy to own the console changes once spec is up.
Sam: Sounds good — I can help with canary automation.
Jen: I'll add telemetry dashboards and a Grafana template.
Maya: Plan to start a staged deploy tomorrow morning. ping @eng-oncall if problems.
